task: Decide whether pUSD (asset 7777) may be enabled in a token catalog with the entry below, relying on the pusd-token-list release approved in the ReleaseRegistry, listed in the VerifiedTokenList and stored on-chain.

steps.description: eth_chainId and compare with the entry
steps.intervention: Know the expected chain ID and compare the hex value by hand.

steps.description: finalized native head, its number, and the EVM block hash for that height
steps.intervention: Know that native and EVM block hashes differ and that ReviveApi.ethBlockHash maps them.

steps.description: native Assets metadata and asset record for 7777 at that block
steps.intervention: Decode SCALE storage with the right runtime types (the asset-fee decoding trap in docs/CHAIN_FINDINGS.md).

steps.description: derive the ERC-20 precompile address of asset 7777
steps.intervention: Know the runtime’s address scheme (u32 big-endian, 12 zero bytes, 00010000) and that it is verified for spec 3002 only.

steps.description: eth_call symbol(), name(), decimals() on the precompile at the EVM block hash
steps.intervention: Encode three selectors and ABI-decode a string, a string and a uint8 by hand.

steps.description: compare the five entry fields with native and EVM values
steps.intervention: Compare five fields across three sources and notice any disagreement.

steps.description: compute the release ID keccak256(abi.encode(owner, bytes32 label))
steps.intervention: Know the registry’s identifier scheme and pack the label as bytes32.

steps.description: eth_call releaseOf and decisionOf on the ReleaseRegistry
steps.intervention: Know the ABI, decode the tuples, and decide whether this reviewer is one you trust.

steps.description: eth_call isListed and entryOf on the VerifiedTokenList and compare with the release
steps.intervention: Know the consumer ABI and check that the entry names the same release, report and reviewer.

steps.description: fetch the block of the stored report, find the remark.store extrinsic, decode the bytes, recompute both hashes
steps.intervention: Locate the extrinsic, decode hex to JSON, recompute blake2-256 of the bytes and the canonical SHA-256 of the report; not feasible by hand without the project’s canonicalization.

steps.description: check the report’s age and the runtime it pinned against the current runtime
steps.intervention: Compare dates by hand and know the current runtime version.
Weigh eleven partial results; nothing records the decision or its basis.

manual.recordOfDecision: none: the maintainer would have to write it down

steps.description: npm run rc -- check_release --release v1.0.1 (the entry against both interfaces, sealed)
node examples/token-catalog/catalog.js acceptance --config examples/token-catalog/config/testnet.json (registry, listing, stored report, runtime, age, policy)

result.line: pUSD     0x00001e6100000000000000000000000000010000  AVAILABLE  valid  report cbd78faa85f8… revision 1

failureDetection.scenario: The same entry with 18 decimals (release v1.0.0).
failureDetection.manual: Detected only if the maintainer compares the decimals in step m6; nothing stops the process otherwise.

steps.description: npm run rc -- check_release --release v1.0.0 (the entry with the Ethereum default of 18 decimals)

result.remediation: Publish a release whose entry uses the chain's decimals (6), then recheck.

scope: Internal validation by the project author on the public testnet nodes. Path M is executed as code so its timings are reproducible; a person performing the same reads with a wallet UI, an explorer and a terminal would be slower at each intervention. Owner, reviewer and operator are the project test account. External adoption and willingness to pay are not measured here.
